title: Protocol to assess metabolic activity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by measuring heat flow using isothermal calorimetry
protocol: Inoculate 5 mL LB from -80°C freeze stock for planktonic cultures.
Shake the culture at 180 rpm for 24 h at 37°C.
Filter the ON culture through a 10 μm syringe filter.
Adjust the OD600 of the filtered culture to 0.005 using a spectrophotometer.
Mix filtered ON culture with alginate for bead production.
Homogenize the mixture thoroughly.
Extrude the homogenized mixture into a CaCl2 solution drop by drop.
Harden alginate beads in stirred CaCl2 solution for 1 hour.
Wash hardened alginate beads and transfer to Erlenmeyer flasks containing LB medium.
Filter an ON culture through a 10 μm syringe filter.
Measure the OD600 of the filtered culture using a spectrophotometer.
Adjust the OD600 to 0.005 by diluting in sterile LB supplemented with 0.2% arabinose.
Add 200 μL of adjusted ON culture into each plastic insert positioned in a standard 48 well plate.
Incubate plates at 37°C and shake at 120 rpm for 24 hours.
Remove media from the wells after incubation.
Wash the wells with sterile saline solution.
Transfer biofilm-containing inserts to titanium vials of calPlate.
Filter the ON culture through a 10 μm syringe filter.
Measure the OD of the filtered ON culture on a spectrophotometer.
Adjust the ON culture to a final OD600 of 0.005 in sterile LB.
Fill the sterile plastic inserts with 200 μL of the adjusted ON culture.
Cover the plastic inserts with parafilm.
Position the covered inserts in a 48-well plate.
Incubate for 24 h at 37°C, 120 rpm to develop biofilm.
Remove planktonic biomass by gently removing supernatant after incubation.
Wash the inserts gently with 200 μL sterile saline solution (0.9% NaCl).
Position the washed inserts into titanium vials of the calPlate™.
Add 200 μL fresh LB media supplemented with 0.2% L-arabinose to each plastic insert.
Filter the ON culture through a 10 μm syringe filter to ensure a mainly planktonic population for encapsulation in alginate beads.
Measure the OD of the filtered ON culture on a spectrophotometer and adjust to an OD600 of 2.
Dilute the OD adjusted culture 20× in a sterile alginate solution (2% w/v) to a final OD600 of 0.1.
Place 150 mL of sterile 0.25 M CaCl₂ in a 250 mL beaker glass on a magnetic stirrer with a sterile magnet (∼3 cm length).
Set the magnetic stirrer to 150 rpm and place a 21-gauge needle perpendicular to- and ∼3 cm from the surface of the CaCl₂ solution, and ∼1.5 cm from the edge of the beaker.
Connect the needle to a 20 mL syringe containing the alginate-bacterial solution by sterile silicone tubing (internal diameter = 2 mm).
Mount the syringe into a syringe pump and set the flow rate to 30 mL/h.
Dispense droplets of the alginate-bacteria solution into the stirred CaCl₂ solution.
Harden the spherical beads for 1 h in the 0.25 M CaCl₂ solution.
Discard the CaCl₂ and wash the beads twice by swirling the beads carefully in 50 mL sterile 0.9% saline solution in a beaker.
Transfer 20 beads to 50 mL prewarmed LB medium in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate at 37°C and 100 rpm for 24 h.
Transfer beads to a new beaker and rinse them gently by swirling in 50 mL 0.9% sterile NaCl for <1 min to remove non-embedded bacteria.
Place a single bead into a plastic insert (calWell™, Symcel AB).
Position plastic inserts into titanium vials of the calPlate™ (Symcel AB, Sweden).
Add 190 μL fresh LB medium supplemented with 0.2% L-arabinose resulting in 200 μL total volume in each well.
Set up the calPlate™ for measurement.
Insert the calPlate™ into the calScreener™ for automatic and continuous measurement of released heat.
Add sterile medium to vials at positions A 1–8 and F 1–8 as thermodynamic references.
Add culture and medium controls separately to vials at sample positions B1–E8.
Transfer samples in plastic inserts into titanium vials placed in the 48 well plastic holder.
Place lids on the titanium vials and close them using a torque wrench.
Fill reference vials with 200 μL LB medium.
Use gloves or sterile tweezers to minimize contamination risk.
For biofilm and alginate bead samples, transfer plastic inserts containing samples into titanium vials on the plate.
For planktonic cultures, place empty plastic inserts into titanium vials on the calPlate™ and add 200 μL aliquots of diluted samples.
Loosely place lids on the vials.
Tighten the lids using a torque wrench set at 40 cNm force.
Check the temperature setting on the temperature control unit; it should be set at 37°C.
Open calView™ software and create a new experiment.
Start data collection before plate insertion.
Place the calPlate in the correct orientation on the bridge.
Push the plate insertion arm to position one and let the system stabilize for 10 minutes.
Push the plate insertion arm to position two and wait for 20 minutes for temperature equilibration of the system.
Push the plate to final position three (measuring position) and activate Reaction Start in calView™.
Retract the plate insertion arm to start position.
Do not move the plate from the sensor when retracting the arm.
Remove calPlate™.
Press Stop in calView™ to end the experiment and save the file for further analysis.
Insert the plate insertion arm completely.
Retrieve the calPlate™ with help of the magnets.
Open the lids using the torque.
Retrieve the sample for further analysis if required, otherwise discard.
Validate data quality.
Check and validate quality of measurement and prepare data for analysis.
Open the experiment file in calView™.
Normalize data with baseline correction (select approx. 20 min in lag phase with signal between 0–10 μW).
Export *.csv file (for analysis in calData, GraphPad, Microsoft Excel or any other compatible software solution).
Check data quality and see if there were any issues with the measurement.
